title: Hank Jones trio, his uncle's family and Tweed Beard
summary: Working on Grand River with Johnny Johnson and Hank Jones, the kindness of his Detroit relatives, and starting with bassist Tweed Beard.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And I worked at a place on Grand River with Johnny Johnson, the drummer, again... And we had a three-piece group: Johnny Johnson, Hank Jones playing piano, and me playing the alto saxophone. And later on, Hank and I, with a guitar player named Al Smith, we organized a little trio. We had it going, had a job booked out in Idaho or someplace, some people were going to send us to Idaho or something...! So my grandmother wanted to come to Detroit again! [LAUGHS] So I had to go back to Jackson and take her back to Detroit again. She wanted to see the family, and my uncle...

But he was... My uncle, I must say again, he was very beautiful to me, and his wife, Lydia, was very beautiful. They had a daughter named Greta. The whole time I stayed with them, they never charged me a penny for anything. And I was out working and making money. They wouldn't let me spend anything, you know. They were so great to me -- and anybody else from the family who wanted to take a shot at Detroit. We had really great times together.

So I brought my grandmother back. And I came back, and things had changed around a little bit. I started working with a bass player out of Columbus, Ohio, named Tweed(?) Beard. And we had a very good group going.
